context: One field has fixed limits; the other's floor is the first field's value, so that floor is not a number the suite can pin once. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats the pair as two independent fields, probes the total budget's floor at whatever daily cap it already had in scope - usually a mid-range one - and stops. The suite then reads as complete while the floor has only ever been exercised at a single position, so a comparison written against a constant instead of against dailyCapCents stays green, and the advertiser complaint about the largest daily cap remains unexplained. The values that discriminate are the floor probed twice: 999 / 1000 / 1001 at dailyCapCents 1000, and 99999 / 100000 / 100001 at dailyCapCents 100000.

checklist.name: Test file created
checklist.description: A file src/campaign.test.js exists and contains at least one test that imports validateCampaign.

checklist.name: Daily cap limits covered on all three points at each end
checklist.description: Daily caps 999 (DAILY_CAP_TOO_LOW), 1000 (accepted), 1001 (accepted), 99999 (accepted), 100000 (accepted), and 100001 (DAILY_CAP_TOO_HIGH) each appear with the correct expectation, with the total budget held at a value comfortably inside its own range. Covering one end fully and the other with only the limit itself caps this at half; covering fewer than four of the six points scores zero.

checklist.name: Moving floor probed at the bottom of the daily cap range
checklist.description: With dailyCapCents at 1000, total budgets 999 (TOTAL_BELOW_DAILY_CAP), 1000 (accepted), and 1001 (accepted) each appear with the correct expectation. Missing 1001 caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.

checklist.name: Moving floor probed again at the top of the daily cap range
checklist.description: With dailyCapCents at 100000, total budgets 99999 (TOTAL_BELOW_DAILY_CAP), 100000 (accepted), and 100001 (accepted) each appear with the correct expectation. This is the criterion the task exists for: probing the floor at only one daily cap - however thoroughly - scores zero here, because a comparison hard-coded against a constant floor passes every such case. Probing a second daily cap that is not at the top of its range but is clearly different from the first (for example 50000) caps this at half.

checklist.name: Total budget ceiling covered on all three points
checklist.description: Total budgets 9999999 (accepted), 10000000 (accepted), and 10000001 (TOTAL_BUDGET_TOO_HIGH) each appear with the correct expectation, with the daily cap held inside its range. Missing 9999999 caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT collapse the pairs into one test
checklist.description: Each pair of values is its own test case, or is generated per-pair by a loop or table-driven helper that yields an individually named case naming both amounts. A single test function asserting every pair in sequence scores zero: the first failing pair hides every later one, and with a floor that moves between cases that is exactly the information needed to localise the bug.

checklist.name: Specific rejection codes asserted
checklist.description: Failing cases assert the exact code - DAILY_CAP_TOO_LOW, DAILY_CAP_TOO_HIGH, TOTAL_BELOW_DAILY_CAP, TOTAL_BUDGET_TOO_HIGH, and the integer-check codes - rather than only that ok is false. Asserting only falsiness scores zero here: a total budget of 999 against a daily cap of 1000 and a daily cap of 999 are different failures that a falsiness-only suite cannot separate.

checklist.name: Pairs are fixed literals
checklist.description: Every probed pair is written as literals or derived arithmetically from the exported MIN_DAILY_CAP / MAX_DAILY_CAP / MAX_TOTAL_BUDGET. Pairs drawn from Math.random or an unseeded generator score zero here, since the floor under test then differs run to run.
